info.title: Maratus API
info.description:
Maratus is a **trigger-to-screen** platform. Your system sends a URL; a Maratus device on the counter shows it as a QR code; your customer scans it with their phone and lands on your content — a receipt, a loyalty sign-up, a payment page, a survey. Maratus never hosts that content: you host it and pass the link.

> **Requests act on real devices.** There is no sandbox. A successful trigger shows a QR code on a physical screen in your store, and pin changes update what idle screens display. Test against a device you control.

## Authentication

Every request needs an API key, sent as a bearer token:

```http
Authorization: Bearer dk_live_...
```

Create keys in the console at [console.maratus.co](https://console.maratus.co) → **API** → **Create API key** (organization owners and admins only). The full key is shown **once**, at creation — store it in a secrets manager. You can revoke a key at any time; revoked keys stop working immediately.

Each key carries one or more **scopes**. A request with a valid key that lacks the endpoint's scope fails with `403 insufficient_scope`.

| Scope | Grants |
|---|---|
| `usage:read` | `GET /usage` |
| `devices:trigger` | `POST /devices/{deviceId}/trigger` |
| `devices:pin` | The pin endpoints: `/devices/{deviceId}/pin`, `/stores/{storeId}/pin`, `/org/pin` |

Grant each integration only the scopes it needs.

## Finding IDs

- **Device ID** (`dev_...`): open the device in the console (**Stores** → store → device). It is listed under *Device details* with a copy button.
- **Store ID** (`str_...`): open the store in the console (**Stores** → store). It is listed under *Store details*.

## Quickstart

Show a QR code on a device:

```bash
curl -X POST https://api.maratus.co/v1/devices/dev_V1StGXR8_Z5jdHi6B-myT/trigger \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer $MARATUS_API_KEY" \
  -H "Content-Type: application/json" \
  -H "Idempotency-Key: $(uuidgen)" \
  -d '{"action": "show_qr", "payload": {"url": "https://example.com/receipt/8812"}}'
```

A `202 Accepted` response means the command was accepted and pushed to the device:

```json
{ "id": "cmd_4Qp0dN7hZk2bWm9xYc1aE", "status": "queued" }
```

## Idempotency

`POST /devices/{deviceId}/trigger` **requires** an `Idempotency-Key` header. Use a fresh unique value (a UUID works well) for each logical trigger, and reuse the same value when retrying that trigger. Once a trigger has been accepted, any later request with the same key returns the original `202` response and does **not** show the QR again — even if the body differs. Keys are scoped to your organization. Failed attempts (`4xx`, `500`, `503`) do not consume the key, so retrying with the same key is safe.

On the pin endpoints the header is **optional** (`PUT` only). Pin updates are naturally idempotent; the key only protects against a retried or concurrent request fanning out duplicate device updates. Reusing a key with a different body returns `422 invalid_request`; reusing it while the first request is still running returns `409 conflict`.

## Rate limits

Each API key may make **120 requests per minute** (fixed one-minute window). Beyond that the API answers `429 rate_limited` with a `Retry-After` header giving the number of seconds to wait.

## Errors

Errors use a single JSON envelope:

```json
{ "error": { "code": "device_offline", "message": "Device is offline or paused." } }
```

Branch on `code`; `message` is human-readable and may change.

| Code | HTTP | Meaning | Retry? |
|---|---|---|---|
| `missing_idempotency_key` | 400 | Trigger sent without an `Idempotency-Key` header. | No — add the header. |
| `unauthorized` | 401 | Missing, malformed, unknown or revoked API key. | No — fix the key. |
| `insufficient_scope` | 403 | The key lacks the scope this endpoint needs. | No — use a key with the scope. |
| `device_not_subscribed` | 403 | The device has no paid subscription and has used its trial triggers. | No — contact Maratus to activate it. |
| `org_archived` | 403 | Your organization is archived; pin changes that would display a QR are blocked. | No — contact Maratus. |
| `device_not_found` | 404 | No device with this ID in your organization. | No — check the ID. |
| `store_not_found` | 404 | No store with this ID in your organization. | No — check the ID. |
| `device_offline` | 409 | The device is paused, or has not checked in for 15 minutes. | Yes, once the device is back online. |
| `conflict` | 409 | Another request with the same `Idempotency-Key` is still in progress. | Yes — after a short delay, with the same key. |
| `invalid_request` | 422 | Malformed JSON, a body that fails validation, or an `Idempotency-Key` reused with a different pin body. | No — fix the request. |
| `rate_limited` | 429 | Over 120 requests/minute for this key. | Yes — after `Retry-After` seconds. |
| `internal_error` | 500 | The command could not be recorded. | Yes — with the same `Idempotency-Key`. |
| `transport_unavailable` | 503 | The device messaging service did not accept the command. Nothing was shown. | Yes — with the same `Idempotency-Key`. |
| `transport_unconfigured` | 503 | Device messaging is not configured on this deployment. | No — contact Maratus. |

An unexpected server fault can also produce a `500` whose body is not this envelope; treat it like `internal_error`.

## Billing

- Every **paid device slot** includes **1,000 triggers per month**, pooled across your organization. Triggers beyond the pool are billed after the fact as overage on your next invoice — overage never blocks a request.
- Only triggers the device acknowledges (the QR was actually shown) count.
- **Pin changes are free** and never count toward your quota.
- A device without a paid subscription gets **50 lifetime trial triggers**. After that, triggers to it fail with `403 device_not_subscribed` until its subscription is paid.

tags.name: Triggers
tags.description: Show a QR code on a device, on demand. Each accepted trigger counts toward your monthly trigger quota once the device acknowledges it.

tags.name: Pins
tags.description: A **pinned QR** is a persistent QR code an idle device shows between triggers — a menu, a feedback form, your website. Pins resolve per device with the precedence **device > store > organization**: a device in `custom` mode shows its own URL; in `inherit` mode it follows its store, which in turn is `custom`, `inherit` (follow the organization pin) or `none`. A level in `none` mode shows no pinned QR. Pin changes are free, take effect immediately on online devices, and are applied to offline devices when they reconnect. Every pin response includes `affectedDevices`: how many devices' displayed QR changed as a result (0 for a no-op).

post.description:
Shows a QR code for the given URL on the device. Requires the `devices:trigger` scope and an `Idempotency-Key` header.

Delivery is **push**: the command is published to the device over its live connection before this call returns. `202 Accepted` means the command was accepted and handed to the device; the device typically renders the QR within a few seconds. The command expires 60 seconds after it is accepted. A trigger that could not be delivered is never shown late — you get `503 transport_unavailable` instead and can retry.

The device must be online (not paused, and seen in the last 15 minutes) and either subscribed or within its 50-trigger trial.

Possible errors: `400 missing_idempotency_key`, `401 unauthorized`, `403 insufficient_scope`, `403 device_not_subscribed`, `404 device_not_found`, `409 device_offline`, `409 conflict`, `422 invalid_request`, `429 rate_limited`, `500 internal_error`, `503 transport_unavailable` (retry), `503 transport_unconfigured` (do not retry).

parameters.name: deviceId
parameters.description: The device ID (`dev_...`), shown on the device page in the console. Must belong to your organization.

parameters.name: Idempotency-Key
parameters.description: Unique value per logical trigger (e.g. a UUID); reuse it when retrying. Once a trigger is accepted, the same key returns the original `202` response without showing the QR again, regardless of the body. Scoped to your organization.

202.description: Accepted and published to the device. Also returned, unchanged, when replaying an `Idempotency-Key` that was already accepted.

400.description: `missing_idempotency_key` — the `Idempotency-Key` header is missing or empty.

403.description: `insufficient_scope` — the key lacks `devices:trigger`; or `device_not_subscribed` — the device has no paid subscription and has used its 50 trial triggers.

error.message: API key lacks the devices:trigger scope.
This device has no active subscription. Contact Maratus to activate it.

404.description: `device_not_found` — no device with this ID in your organization.

409.description: `device_offline` — the device is paused or has not checked in for 15 minutes; or `conflict` — a request with the same `Idempotency-Key` is in flight (retry shortly with the same key).

422.description: `invalid_request` — malformed JSON, unknown `action`, or `payload.url` is not an http(s) URL of at most 2048 characters.

error.message: payload.url must be an http(s) URL ≤ 2048 chars.

500.description: `internal_error` — the command could not be recorded. Nothing was sent; retry with the same `Idempotency-Key`.

503.description: `transport_unavailable` — the device messaging service did not accept the command; nothing was shown and the key was released, so retry with the same `Idempotency-Key`. `transport_unconfigured` — device messaging is not configured on this deployment; retrying will not help.

error.message: Could not reach the device transport. Retry.
The device transport is not configured on this deployment. Retrying will not help.

put.description:
Send `{"url": ...}` to pin a URL on this device (mode becomes `custom`), or `{"mode": "inherit" | "none"}` to follow the store/organization pin or show no pinned QR. Re-sending the device's current URL is a no-op (`affectedDevices: 0`). Requires the `devices:pin` scope. Free.

Archived organizations can only switch to `none`; setting a URL or `inherit` returns `403 org_archived`.

parameters.name: deviceId
parameters.description: The device ID (`dev_...`), shown on the device page in the console. Must belong to your organization.

parameters.name: Idempotency-Key
parameters.description: Optional. Guards a retried or concurrent request against fanning out duplicate device updates. A completed request's response is replayed for the same key and body; the same key with a different body returns `422 invalid_request`; while the first request is still running, `409 conflict`. Keys are scoped per endpoint type (device, store, org pins).

mode.description: `inherit` follows the next level up; `none` shows no pinned QR. (`custom` is set by sending `url`.)

200.description: The device's pin state after the change.

404.description: `device_not_found` — no device with this ID in your organization.

delete.summary: Reset a device's pin to inherit
delete.description: Clears the device's own pin and sets it to `inherit`, so it follows its store/organization pin — it is **not** guaranteed to go blank (use `PUT {"mode": "none"}` for that). Same as `PUT {"mode": "inherit"}`. Idempotent. Requires the `devices:pin` scope. Free. Returns `403 org_archived` for archived organizations.

parameters.name: deviceId
parameters.description: The device ID (`dev_...`), shown on the device page in the console. Must belong to your organization.

200.description: The device's pin state after the reset (`pinMode` is always `inherit`, `pin` is always `null`).

404.description: `device_not_found` — no device with this ID in your organization.

put.description:
Send `{"url": ...}` to pin a URL for the store (mode becomes `custom`), or `{"mode": "inherit" | "none"}` to follow the organization pin or show no pinned QR. Applies to the store's devices that are in `inherit` mode; devices with their own `custom` or `none` pin are unaffected. Re-sending the current state is a no-op (`affectedDevices: 0`). Requires the `devices:pin` scope. Free.

Archived organizations can only switch to `none`; setting a URL or `inherit` returns `403 org_archived`.

parameters.name: storeId
parameters.description: The store ID (`str_...`), shown on the store page in the console. Must belong to your organization.

parameters.name: Idempotency-Key
parameters.description: Optional. Guards a retried or concurrent request against fanning out duplicate device updates. A completed request's response is replayed for the same key and body; the same key with a different body returns `422 invalid_request`; while the first request is still running, `409 conflict`. Keys are scoped per endpoint type (device, store, org pins).

mode.description: `inherit` follows the next level up; `none` shows no pinned QR. (`custom` is set by sending `url`.)

200.description: The store's pin state after the change.

404.description: `store_not_found` — no store with this ID in your organization.

delete.summary: Reset a store's pin to inherit
delete.description: Clears the store's own pin and sets it to `inherit`, so its inheriting devices follow the organization pin, if any. Same as `PUT {"mode": "inherit"}`. Idempotent. Requires the `devices:pin` scope. Free. Returns `403 org_archived` for archived organizations.

parameters.name: storeId
parameters.description: The store ID (`str_...`), shown on the store page in the console. Must belong to your organization.

200.description: The store's pin state after the reset (`pinMode` is always `inherit`, `pin` is always `null`).

404.description: `store_not_found` — no store with this ID in your organization.

put.description: Pins a URL for the whole organization. It is shown by every device that resolves to the organization level (device and store both in `inherit` mode). The organization level has no modes — send `{"url": ...}` only; `mode` returns `422 invalid_request`. Re-sending the current URL is a no-op (`affectedDevices: 0`). Requires the `devices:pin` scope. Free. Returns `403 org_archived` for archived organizations.

parameters.name: Idempotency-Key
parameters.description: Optional. Guards a retried or concurrent request against fanning out duplicate device updates. A completed request's response is replayed for the same key and body; the same key with a different body returns `422 invalid_request`; while the first request is still running, `409 conflict`. Keys are scoped per endpoint type (device, store, org pins).

200.description: The organization pin after the change.

delete.description: Removes the organization pin. Devices that resolved to it show no pinned QR. Idempotent — clearing when no pin is set succeeds with `affectedDevices: 0`. Allowed for archived organizations. Requires the `devices:pin` scope. Free.

200.description: The organization pin after clearing (`pin` is always `null`).

error.message: API key lacks the devices:pin scope.

get.description:
Returns how many triggers your organization's devices acknowledged (the QR was shown) for commands created since the start of the current **UTC calendar month**. Pin changes are not counted. Requires the `usage:read` scope.

This is an operational counter. Billing periods are anniversary-based (they start on your subscription date, not the 1st of the month), so this number is not the figure on your invoice.

200.description: Trigger usage for the current UTC calendar month.

error.message: API key lacks the usage:read scope.

Unauthorized.description: `unauthorized` — the `Authorization` header is missing or malformed, or the key is unknown or revoked.

RateLimited.description: `rate_limited` — more than 120 requests in the current minute for this key. Wait `Retry-After` seconds.

PinForbidden.description: `insufficient_scope` — the key lacks `devices:pin`; or `org_archived` — your organization is archived and this change would display a QR.

error.message: API key lacks the devices:pin scope.

PinInvalid.description: `invalid_request` — malformed JSON, both `url` and `mode` sent, an invalid `mode`, a `url` that is not an absolute http(s) URL of at most 2048 characters, or an `Idempotency-Key` already used with a different body.

IdempotencyInProgress.description: `conflict` — a request with the same `Idempotency-Key` is still in progress. Retry shortly with the same key.

error.message: A request with this Idempotency-Key is still in progress.

Error.description: Error envelope returned by every failing request.

code.description: Stable, machine-readable error code — branch on this. See the Errors table in the introduction for every code.

message.description: Human-readable explanation. May change; do not parse.

TriggerAction.title: TriggerAction
TriggerAction.description:
What the device does when triggered. Each action defines the `payload` it expects.

| Value | Effect | Payload |
|---|---|---|
| `show_qr` | Shows `payload.url` as a QR code, then returns to the idle screen after the organization's QR timeout. | `{ "url": "https://…" }` |

New actions may be added over time; treat unknown values in responses as opaque.

x-enumDescriptions.show_qr: Show payload.url as a QR code until the QR timeout elapses.

url.description: Absolute `http` or `https` URL (at most 2048 characters) that the device shows as a QR code. You host this content.

id.description: ID of the device command created for this trigger (`cmd_...`).

status.description: Always `queued`: accepted and published to the device.

PinUrlValue.description: Absolute `http` or `https` URL (at most 2048 characters) to show as the pinned QR code.

PinUrl.description: A pinned URL and when it was set.

pinnedAt.description: When this URL was pinned (ISO 8601, UTC). Re-sending the same URL keeps the original timestamp. Always set for device pins; may be `null` for store and organization pins in rare legacy cases.

PinMode.description: `custom` — shows its own pinned URL. `inherit` — follows the level above (device → store → organization). `none` — shows no pinned QR.

pin.description: The device's own pinned URL. Set only when `pinMode` is `custom`; otherwise `null`.

effectiveUrl.description: The URL the device now shows while idle, after resolving device > store > organization. `null` when no pinned QR applies.

affectedDevices.description: How many devices' displayed QR changed (0 or 1 here; 0 for a no-op).

pin.description: The store's own pinned URL. Set only when `pinMode` is `custom`; otherwise `null`.

affectedDevices.description: How many of the store's devices had their displayed QR changed (0 for a no-op).

pin.description: The organization pin, or `null` after clearing.

affectedDevices.description: How many devices had their displayed QR changed (0 for a no-op).

activations_this_month.description: Acknowledged triggers for commands created in `period`. Not an invoice figure — billing periods are anniversary-based.

start.description: First instant of the month (inclusive), ISO 8601 UTC.

end.description: First instant of the next month (exclusive), ISO 8601 UTC.
